Prime Minister Narendra Modi travels on the Namma Metro with Karnataka's Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda after inaugurating the elevated stretch of the Pink Line on November 13, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
Infrastructure development and improved connectivity play a crucial role in the country’s economic growth, creating new opportunities for employment, industry and progress, said Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Addressing an event in Bengaluru after inaugurating the elevated section of the Pink Line of Namma Metro on Friday, Mr. Modi said that better connectivity enables development opportunities to reach every section of society, thereby strengthening the fight against poverty.
Earlier in the day, referring to a recent World Bank report, he said nearly 50 crore Indians had come out of “extreme poverty” over the past 12 to 13 years. He attributed this progress to expanding development opportunities, speaking after the inauguration of Namma Metro pink line.
Describing Bengaluru as India’s Silicon Valley and a major engine of innovation and economic growth, Mr. Modi said the Centre was prioritising the region’s development and modern public infrastructure. He added that metro expansion reflected the government’s commitment to improving ease of living and travel, particularly for middle-class families.
He said the projects launched in Karnataka would strengthen Bengaluru’s identity as a technology city and accelerate the State’s contribution towards building a developed India.
He inaugurated the Bengaluru - Mangaluru - Madgaon Vande Bharat train as well. He said Karnataka had recently received its first Vande Bharat Sleeper train and had now received another Vande Bharat service connecting the State with Goa. The new service, he said, would provide passengers, including those travelling from Bengaluru and the coastal region, with a semi-high-speed travel experience.
Mr. Modi announced four additional Amrit Bharat railway stations and two projects involving railway track doubling and electrification in Karnataka. More than 60 railway stations in Karnataka have been selected for redevelopment under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme, he said. Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur, and Subramanya were among the stations identified for upgrades.
The Prime Minister highlighted three energy-related projects in Karnataka, including an expanded LPG bottling plant, a marketing terminal and a compressed biogas (CBG) plant in Bengaluru, he inaugurated on Friday, to be part of efforts to strengthen India’s energy security.
The CBG plant on the Karnataka Compost Development Corporation (KCDC) premises in Bengaluru is expected to produce around 13 tonnes of biogas daily. Mr. Modi said the facility would support better waste management while helping reduce dependence on imported natural gas.
